No. Treat a saved-view JSON document as untrusted input every time it is replayed, not as trusted merely because it was previously stored. Persisting it is fine; concatenating its fields, operators, sort directions, or values into SQL is not.

## Saved views

Compile the JSON through a small, server-owned query DSL:
- Map public field tokens (for example, status, createdAt) to fixed SQL/Query Builder expressions; never accept raw column names, relationship paths, JSON paths, SQL fragments, or ORDER BY text.
- Allowlist operators per field and type—e.g., status: eq/in, createdAt: gte/lte; validate arity, scalar/array types, bounds, date formats, list sizes, and nesting/complexity.
- Bind every literal as a parameter. OWASP recommends prepared statements and says identifiers and sort-order indicators, which cannot be bound, require allowlisting or query redesign. Laravel explicitly notes that PDO cannot bind column names and warns not to let user input dictate query columns, including order by columns. OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
- Re-authorize the current user against every object/scope referenced when executing the view; do not rely on the creator’s historical rights. Laravel policies organize authorization around the current user and resource, and persistent middleware is specifically useful when permissions change after initial rendering.
- Version the view grammar/schema. Reject unknown versions and unknown keys/operators by default, rather than silently interpreting an old payload under new semantics. This rejection policy and fresh authorization are design inferences, not a claim prescribed verbatim by OWASP or Laravel.

## Retries and digests

Write notification intent into a transactional outbox in the same database transaction as the business change: recipient/scope, template version, payload snapshot or immutable reference, scheduled time, and a stable delivery key. A worker then claims and sends it. AWS documents the transactional outbox as the answer to the distributed “dual write” problem.
Use a stable key such as notification:{event_id}:{recipient_id}:{channel}:{template_version} across retries, and enforce it in your delivery ledger and, where supported, pass it as a provider idempotency/deduplication key. AWS warns that standard SQS can deliver messages more than once and says consumers must be idempotent; retry-with-backoff likewise requires idempotent operations.
At send time, re-check current notification preferences, consent, tenant membership, quiet hours, suppression, and cancellation/revocation state. For digests, atomically claim eligible items into a digest batch, so retries resend the same batch rather than accidentally adding later events. These are design inferences based on durable-state and idempotency principles.
Finally, model provider timeout/connection-loss after request submission as unknown, not failed: the provider may have accepted and delivered it. Persist attempt IDs, request/idempotency keys, response evidence, and reconciliation status; retry only through the same stable key or provider lookup. AWS’s SNS FIFO documentation shows deduplication IDs suppress repeated accepted publishes only within a five-minute window—useful, but not a universal end-to-end delivery guarantee.

Sources:
1. [OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)
2. [Laravel Query Builder](https://laravel.com/docs/master/queries)
3. [Laravel Authorization](https://laravel.com/docs/authorization)
4. [Laravel Livewire Security](https://livewire.laravel.com/docs/4.x/security)
5. [AWS Transactional Outbox](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/cloud-design-patterns/transactional-outbox.html)
6. [AWS SQS at-least-once delivery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues-at-least-once-delivery.html)
7. [AWS Retry with Backoff](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/cloud-design-patterns/retry-backoff.html)
8. [AWS SNS FIFO deduplication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/fifo-message-dedup.html)
